subject: Request: service surface decomposition + isolation map for SOC 2 / SIG
messages:
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@lumos.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@lumos.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: service surface decomposition + isolation map for SOC 2 / SIG

Hi Aisha / Kimberly,

We're starting the SOC 2 and SIG collection for our upcoming audit window and need a clear, consumable artifact that describes Redwood's service surface decomposition for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically Lumos needs: 

- A high-level network diagram that shows control plane vs data plane boundaries for both Dedicated (Redwood-managed infra) and Private (customer VPC / on-prem) modes.
- An isolation matrix that lists tenant-facing endpoints, allowed egress patterns, and which components handle secrets/keys.
- A short narrative (1–2 pages) explaining how fallbacks and model variants are routed when Dedicated capacity is constrained (this helps our auditor understand graceful degradation).

Deadline: 2027-08-20 (audit intake). Can you confirm what you can provide and by when? Attaching a short ask brief.

Thanks,
Alice
Security Programs Manager
Lumos Financial

Attachments: lumos-ask-brief.pdf (1 page)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@lumos.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: service surface decomposition + isolation map for SOC 2 / SIG

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver a compact evidence pack that meets the audit intake. Proposed plan: 

1) By 2027-08-13: internal draft artifacts (diagrams + matrix + 1-page narrative) for internal review.
2) By 2027-08-15: finalized artifacts and a single .zip deliverable with SVG/PNG diagrams, CSV isolation matrix, and a short writeup.
3) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough the week of 8/16 for your auditors.

Owners: I'll coordinate diagrams and narrative; Kimberly will validate network controls and egress rules; Vivek will confirm control-plane boundaries and KMS/HSM handling.

Sending an initial set of attachments internally (svc-surface-decomp-v1.svg + isolation-matrix-v1.csv) as a starting point. Will iterate quickly.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Direct: (555) 215-0193

Attachments (internal): svc-surface-decomp-v1.svg (draft), isolation-matrix-v1.csv (draft)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: service surface decomposition + isolation map for SOC 2 / SIG

Kimberly / Vivek — forwarding Alice's ask and attaching the first-pass artifacts. Two quick asks inline: 

- Kimberly: can you review the "egress classifications" column in isolation-matrix-v1.csv and flag any endpoints that should be No-Egress or require customer approval? I marked some as 'restricted-ops' but want your confirmation.
- Vivek: control-plane callouts — please confirm which services are in Redwood's control plane (control-plane-hosting, orchestration, model registry index) versus customer-managed (VPC connectors, KMS in private mode). I added a note in the SVG labeled "P1" but that needs verify.

Also: I opened JIRA ticket JIRA-842 to track follow-ups and packaging for the Sig/CAIQ artifacts.

Thanks — aim to close internal review by end-of-day 2027-08-13.

-- Aisha

Aisha / Vivek — reviewed the CSV and left inline comments. Summary: 

- Marked 3 endpoints as "no-egress" for Dedicated: admin-metrics, infra-health, kv-sync (these only talk to internal control plane subnets).
- For Private: clarified that customer VPC egress is governed by their own NAT/GW — we should explicitly call this out in the narrative to avoid auditor confusion.
- Added a control-plane callout PNG to highlight KMS responsibilities (see attachment).

Small edits in the SVG too: added dashed boundary for "model-variant-fallback" routing so auditors can see the fallback path when Dedicated bursts.

Kimberly

Redwood Inference
